added_lines: . Congratulations Redwood NS: Redwood NS made history winning their first solo County Final. In a hard fought game, in very wet conditions on Tuesday 10th Nov. , Redwood emerged victorious against a gallant Barnane side. It was a very entertaining and at times tense game for spectators. Captain Tommy Houlihan accepted the plaque on behalf of Redwood NS, County Football Champions. Redwood NS would like to thank Richie Bourke for leading the team to their success. Redwood Community Variety Show takes place in Redwood Church on Wednesday 25th November at 7pm. There is a fantastic line up of entertainment on the night including : Pete Kennedy, Daniel Maher, Noreen & Donal Ryan, Denis Duffy, Sarah Moran, Midlife Crisis, Ruth Morrisey & Brian Hourigan, Anne Marie Hough, Redwood Parents Singing Group and the Children of Redwood on the night Hubie Hogan. Tea and refreshments and a raffle (inaid of Redwood School, Redwood Church & The Samaritans) will be held in Redwood School immediately afterwards. All are welcome to this wonderful community event. Free admission for all. Reflection Christ is our King, not because he rules with power, but because his love is present in every part of our lives. We are all created in God's image and carry his l ight within us. When we take time to pray, we become more aware of this presence and recognise the many ways God works through the people around us. Jesus reminds us that the Kingdom of God is among us. It is not something we to wait for; it is here and now, in every act of kindness, every moment of love and every helping hand. As we celebrate Christ the King, may we open our hearts to God's presence and bring his love and light to others. Lorrha and Dorrha

Martin, Joan and Mary MOTHER TERESA : When Mother Teresa accepted the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo in 1979, part of her acceptance speech went like this: “It is not enough for us to say: ‘I love God, but I do not love my neighbour.’ Saint John says that you are a liar if you say you love God and you don’t love your neighbour. (I John 4:20) How can you love God whom you do not see, if you do not love your neighbour whom you see, whom you touch, with whom you live? And so this is very important for us to realize that love, to be true, has to hurt.” REFLECTION : Jesus is the Hungry – to be fed. Jesus is the Thirsty – to be satiated. Jesus is the Naked – to be clothed. Jesus is the Homeless – to be taken in. Jesus is the Sick – to be healed. Jesus is the Lonely – to be loved. Jesus is the Unwanted – to be wanted. Jesus is the Leper – to wash his wounds. Jesus is the Beggar – to give him a smile. Jesus is the Drunkard – to listen to him. Jesus is the Mental – to protect him. Jesus is the Little One – to embrace him. Jesus is the Blind – to lead him. Jesus is the Dumb – to speak for him. Jesus is the Crippled – to walk with him. Jesus is the Drug Addict – to befriend him. Jesus is the Prostitute – to remove from danger and befriend her. Jesus is the Prisoner – to be visited. Jesus is the Old – to be served. Mass in Friday MASS: 6 p.m. Saturday in Miltown Grouped Anniversary Masses Michael Fitzpatrick, Main Street Mary Higgins (McGee) Main St. & A, John & May Smyth & their Daughter Nuala Kelly Marian Lynch, Clonbony Mary & Siney Talty & Deceased Members of the Talty Family, Carhuduff Paddy McCaw & Deceased Members of the McCaw Family Denis & Mary Curtin, Son John, Daughter Mary & Grand Daughter Sharon Thady Boohan & Deceased Members of The Boohan Family, Ballard Road MASS: 12.15 Sunday in Miltown for Michael Doyle, Spanish Point (1st Anniversary) MOY : MASS: 9.15 Sunday in Moy Grouped Anniversary Masses Eileen & Patrick Devitt their Son Michael & Deceased Members of The Vaughan & Devitt Families Pat & Mary Commane, Aylebrack REFLECTION : You entrusted me with two talents; Here are two more I have made.
We are familiar with the story of the boy who wanted to bring a gift to Jesus at his birth.
He saw others bringing expensive gifts of Gold, frankincense and myrrh; He wondered what he had to offer, and thought of his drum, and how he could play a song for Jesus, Mary and Joseph.
A simple story, and isn’t it true about our gifts and talents?

Each of us has different qualities, gifts: all are given by God and are valued in God’s love: gifts of music, sport and art, of conversation and humour, of compassion and leadership; Gifts of friendship, prayer and caring for others, of listening and encouraging; whatever your gift, your talent; your gift of being a caring parent, of being able to help a younger generation in any way; be grateful, each of us has a ‘bit of God’ within us: and each of us can offer to God in our love and care for others what he has given to us.

He looks on us, and loves each of us; sees us as we are and loves us, sees us as we can be and calls each of us, in our own personality and talents, to grow in love, to offer our talents in his service, and to become more like him.
